title: Adjunction-preserving quotient-to-pushforward support model
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Use ordinary sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], on small representatives of the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Derived categories are unbounded localizations at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] and a closed immersion $a:C\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], write $j:T\setminus C\hookrightarrow T$ for its open complement and set
$$Q^\tau_{T,C}=\operatorname{coker}(j_!\underline A_{T\setminus C}\longrightarrow\underline A_T),\qquad \tau=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet},$$
where the arrow is induced by inclusion of the open object into the final object and extension by zero is [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Denote the quotient map by $r^\tau_{T,C}$. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with closed immersions $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, $j:W\hookrightarrow Y$. Put $P=X\times_kY$, $S=Z\times_kW$, $h=i\times_kj$ and let $p_X,p_Y$ be the projections [def-pc-base-change]. For any one of these closed pairs $a:C\hookrightarrow T$, put
$$E_a^\tau(V)=Q^\tau_{T,C}\otimes_A^L\underline V_T,\qquad V\in D(A),$$
using the termwise constant sheaf and derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor, def-weil-derived-tensor]. Equip $E_a^\tau\dashv H_a^\tau=R\Gamma_C(T_\tau,-)$ [def-pur-support-cohomology] with the adjunction induced by the ordinary bijection sending $\sigma:Q^\tau_{T,C}\otimes_A\underline V_T\to F$ to $v\mapsto\sigma(\overline1\otimes v)$. Let $C_a(V)=a_*\underline V_C$. In the etale topology let $e_a:\underline V_T\to C_a(V)$ be the normalized quotient map of [def-pur-supported-exterior-product], and in the pro-etale topology let $q_a:\underline V_T\to C_a(V)$ be the normalized quotient map of [def-pur-proetale-supported-exterior-product]. There is a unique natural isomorphism $\beta_a:E_a^\tau\cong C_a$ compatible with the specified adjunctions to the same right adjoint $H_a^\tau$ (the comparison on that right adjoint is the identity). It is the derived extension of the ordinary-module isomorphism whose components carry $r_a\otimes1$ to $e_a$ in the etale case and to $q_a$ in the pro-etale case. It is natural in $V$, preserves the quotient-generator maps, and identifies these adjunctions and their derived evaluation counits.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4: identify the quotient support model with the normalized closed-pushforward support model and its counit.

proof.text: We check the hypotheses of the open–closed sequences. The field $k$ is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0,(1)$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X,Y$ Noetherian. The scheme $P$ is finite type over $k$: finite affine covers of $X,Y$ give a finite cover of $P$ by spectra of $B\otimes_kD$, generated over $k$ by generators of $B$ and $D$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Thus $P$ too is Noetherian. The open complement of each closed pair is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Moreover every intersection of this complement with an affine open of its ambient scheme is Noetherian and hence quasi-compact, so the open immersion is quasi-compact. The ambient schemes are quasi-separated: $X,Y$ have closed diagonals by separatedness [def-weil-proper-morphism]; the diagonal of $P$ is the product of their diagonals, hence closed (on product affine charts its defining equations are the two sets of diagonal equations). A closed immersion is quasi-compact since its inverse image of an affine open is a closed affine subscheme. Consequently the pro-etale open–closed sequence below has its required qcqs ambient scheme and quasi-compact open immersion.

source.place: Paragraph 4: checking the geometric hypotheses of the quotient identification.

proof.text: For each pair $a:C\hookrightarrow T$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] to $A_T$ in the etale topology, and [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf](3) to $B=M=A_T$ in the pro-etale topology. The latter hypotheses were verified in step 1. Both sequences identify the cokernel of $v_!A_{T\setminus C}\to A_T$ with $a_*A_C$, under the unit of inverse image/direct image and the constant inverse-image identification. These are exactly the normalized maps $e_a$ and $q_a$ in [def-pur-supported-exterior-product] and [def-pur-proetale-supported-exterior-product]. The cokernel universal property therefore gives a unique isomorphism $b_{a,A}:Q^\tau_{T,C}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_a(A)$ with $b_{a,A}r_a=e_a$ or $q_a$. Indeed factor the two cokernel maps through one another; both composites are identities since their precompositions with the respective epimorphisms are identities.

Put $B_a(M)=Q^\tau_{T,C}\otimes_{A_T}\underline M_T$. Both $B_a$ and $C_a$ preserve small coproducts and cokernels. For $B_a$, the constant-sheaf functor is left adjoint to sections as stated in [def-pur-supported-exterior-product]; the same sheafification universal property applies in either topology [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Tensoring with $Q^\tau_{T,C}$ is left adjoint by [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. For $C_a$, its normalized adjunction is stated by the two support-product definitions. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] to these adjoints. Thus $b_{a,A}$ and the tensor unit induce $B_a(A^{(I)})\cong C_a(A^{(I)})$ for every set $I$. These maps commute with every map between free modules: on each basis element a free-module map is a finite linear combination of basis elements, and both functors and $b_{a,A}$ respect addition and multiplication by $A$.

source.place: Paragraph 4: extending the normalized rank-one comparison to free coefficients.

proof.text: Present an arbitrary $A$-module $M$ by $A^{(R)}\to A^{(|M|)}\to M\to0$: the second map sends $[m]$ to $m$, and $R$ consists of the relations $[m]+[n]-[m+n]$, $a[m]-[am]$, and $[0]$. Every formal sum reduces modulo these relations to the symbol for its value, so they generate exactly the kernel. A module map sends each generator and relation to the corresponding generator and relation, making this presentation functorial. Apply $B_a,C_a$ and the free-module comparisons of step 3. Taking cokernels gives an isomorphism $b_{a,M}:B_a(M)\cong C_a(M)$, natural in $M$. The equality $b_{a,M}(r_a\otimes1)=e_a$ or $q_a$ follows on each generator $[m]$ from step 2, then descends to the cokernel. Conversely such equality determines $b_{a,M}$, since $r_a\otimes1$ is an epimorphism: tensor preserves cokernels by its left adjoint in [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. No flatness of $M$ is needed.

source.place: Paragraph 4: the functorial cokernel calculation for arbitrary coefficients.

proof.text: The functor $C_a$ is exact in each topology, as stated in the two support-product definitions; hence $B_a\cong C_a$ is exact. For a complex $V$, choose a flat-term K-flat module resolution $P\to V$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the one-point ringed site $(\{*\},A)$. The termwise constant-sheaf functor is exact: constant presheaves are exact since evaluation on every object is exact, and module sheafification is exact [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact]; so $\underline P_T\to\underline V_T$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The constant sheaf complex $\underline P_T$ is K-flat with flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], applied to the morphism of ringed topoi to the point with constant coefficient ring $A_T$. Its module pullback is the constant sheaf functor: sheafifying the constant presheaf is the inverse image from sets to sheaves, with ring structure map the identity [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Therefore, using symmetry and the K-flat definition of derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor, def-weil-derived-tensor], $E_a^\tau(V)$ is represented by $B_a(P)$. The degreewise maps $b_{a,P^n}$ commute with differentials by their naturality, giving $B_a(P)\cong C_a(P)$. Exactness of $C_a$ makes $C_a(P)\to C_a(V)$ a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. This constructs $\beta_a$. These comparisons commute with chain maps and inverses of quasi-isomorphisms, so they are independent of the resolution and natural on the derived category. The degreewise generator equality in step 4 gives the derived generator equality as well.

source.place: Paragraph 4: deriving the normalized comparison on unbounded coefficient complexes.

proof.text: For an ordinary sheaf $F$ and module $M$, precompose $f:C_a(M)\to F$ with $b_{a,M}$ and then with $r_a\otimes1$. Step 4 identifies the resulting map with $f e_a$ or $f q_a$. The normalization clauses of the two support-product definitions say precisely that its constant-sheaf adjoint is the supported-section map $M\to\Gamma_C(T,F)$ followed by the kernel inclusion in $\Gamma(T,F)$. Thus the two ordinary adjunction bijections agree under $b_a$. For a complex $V$ and a K-injective sheaf representative $I$ of $F$, which exists on the small site by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], use [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] to apply this equality on the homotopy categories. Since $C_a\cong B_a$ is exact, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] makes $\Gamma_C(I)$ K-injective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] on both sides of the homotopy adjunction: its Hom sets become $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T)}(C_a(V),F)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(V,H_a^\tau F)$. The equality of the two Hom bijections persists. K-injective computation and the derived adjunctions are the ones specified by the two support-product definitions. Their counits are the inverse images of $1_{H_a^\tau F}$ under these bijections [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection], so $\epsilon_E=\epsilon_C\circ\beta_{H_a^\tau F}$; likewise their units agree after the comparison.

source.place: Paragraph 4: the equality of normalized ordinary and derived adjunction bijections.

proof.text: Finally any adjunction-preserving comparison $b:E_a^\tau\to C_a$ must satisfy, for every $V$, that the adjunct of $b_V$ under $E_a^\tau\dashv H_a^\tau$ is the adjunct of $1_{C_a(V)}$ under $C_a\dashv H_a^\tau$. The adjunction bijection is injective, so $b_V$ is uniquely determined and equals $\beta_{a,V}$. The ordinary uniqueness and quotient-generator equality were verified in step 4, and step 5 derives that equality on every complex. This proves uniqueness with the specified adjunction normalization, as well as naturality and the evaluation-counit assertion.

source.place: Paragraph 4: uniqueness of the comparison with identity on the common right adjoint.

proof_origin.place: The imported paragraph 4 is supplemented by the open–closed quotient argument and the explicit etale/pro-etale support-model definitions.

split_report.summary: Split the rank-one quotient using the existing etale and pro-etale open–closed sequences; extended it to arbitrary modules using free presentations and colimit-preserving adjoints; constructed the unbounded derived comparison using K-flat constant pullback; checked the derived Hom bijections on K-injectives. Corrected uniqueness to explicitly require preservation of the specified adjunctions with identity on their common right adjoint: ordinary-module components alone do not determine a natural transformation on a derived category.
